subject: EU telemetry supplier scope verification and onshore fallback
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@aurionhealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@aurionhealth.com
Date: Tue, 21 Nov 2028 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: EU telemetry supplier scope verification and onshore fallback

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for taking this. As part of our vendor security review, can you confirm the current telemetry/logging supplier Redwood uses for EU customers (the product that receives application telemetry, traces, and usage logs)? Specifically we need:

- The subprocessor name and role (full roster entry)
- Whether telemetry ingestion or any log processing occurs outside of the EU (and if so, where)
- Any temporary/contractor access to telemetry for beta testing (yes/no + controls)
- An outline of onshore fallback options if the supplier routes data outside EU (how would Redwood keep data in EU)

If you can share the latest subprocessor roster and a short attestation on minimal-privilege access and retention practices for telemetry logs, that would get our procurement/legal comfortable. Our timelines are tight — we'd like to complete this by next week.

Thanks,
Oliver Grant
Senior Security Engineer
Aurion Health

Attachments: none
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@aurionhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Nov 2028 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: EU telemetry supplier scope verification and onshore fallback

Hi Oliver — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Kimberly (legal) and Naomi (privacy ops) to cover attestation and retention.

Quick answers up front:
- Primary telemetry processor: TelemetryOne (subprocessor entry included).
- Current processing: ingestion and enrichment occur in EU regions by default; TelemetryOne has an optional U.S. analytics service that is not enabled for EU accounts unless customers opt in.
- Temporary contractor/beta access: we occasionally enable short-lived support access for TelemetryOne engineering in the US during incident triage; access is timeboxed, logged, and requires approval.
- Onshore fallback: Redwood can route telemetry for EU customers to our onshore fallback pool (on-prem/VPC or EU-only managed path). Details in attached spreadsheet.

I'm attaching: redwood_subprocessor_roster_20281128.csv (roster snapshot), onshore_fallback_matrix_aurion_20281128.xlsx (matrix with routing options and steps). Naomi — can you confirm retention/privilege language we can provide as the attestation? Kimberly — can legal sign off on the minimal-privilege attestation and DocuSign addendum if they want a contractual note?

Hannah Schmitt
Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_subprocessor_roster_20281128.csv (roster), onshore_fallback_matrix_aurion_20281128.xlsx (fallback matrix)

Thanks Hannah — the quick summary is helpful and we received the attachments. A couple follow-ups from our side:

1) Can you confirm whether any PII-equivalent log content (e.g., user identifiers linked to patient IDs) is ever sent to TelemetryOne’s U.S. analytics service? We need an explicit no, or a description of safeguards.

2) For the temporary contractor access you mentioned, can you share the approval process (who signs off) and whether those sessions are recorded/audited?

3) The onshore fallback matrix looks promising — procurement would like a high-level runbook we can include in our DPA addendum: trigger conditions, RTO, and contact for cutover. If you can draft a one-page runbook we can attach to the order, that'd be ideal.

Finally, are you open to a short attestation e-signed by Redwood legal that TelemetryOne will not enable U.S. analytics on Aurion's tenancy without written consent? That resolves a lot of our review items.

Appreciate the help — Oliver

Hi Oliver,

Thanks for the clarifying questions — and thanks Hannah/Naomi for the materials. Below are the items we can provide immediately and the contractual language we are prepared to e-sign: 

1) PII-equivalent logs: Redwood confirms TelemetryOne is configured so that Aurion Health tenancies do not route telemetry to TelemetryOne’s U.S. analytics pipeline by default. We will not enable U.S. analytics for Aurion without written authorization from your procurement/legal contact.

2) Temporary access: Any time-limited support access to TelemetryOne engineering requires: (a) request in the incident ticket, (b) approval from Redwood Security lead (Hannah or delegate), (c) pre-defined scope and time window, and (d) session audit logs retained for 12 months. We can include this process as an appendix to the DPA.

3) Runbook: Attached is a 1-page runbook summary (embedded in the onshore fallback matrix) with trigger conditions, RTO targets, and primary contacts for cutover. If Aurion needs a tailored RTO, we can include it in the procurement addendum.

4) Next steps and DocuSign: We've prepared an addendum with the attestation language and the onshore fallback runbook. If that works, we'll send a DocuSign link for signature (DOCUSIGN-ADDENDUM-23871).

Kimberly Park
